title: VEL-VIV-CELEB-GS-01 - Katie x Sofia quiet luxury (greenscreen)
summary: BUILT 2026-08-31 - three finished ads, creator-only A/B/C, 58.5s each, 1080x1920. The Vivienne sold the way the reference sells Brad Pitt: the celebrity is the MECHANISM, not decoration. It never claims either woman carries ours - it claims the LOOK is theirs, prices that look at ten thousand dollars, then hands over the affordable route. Combo hook: Katie still, Sofia still, 4.6s total, then we are on our bag for the rest of the ad. Timecodes below are the REAL ones, taken from the voiceover's own word alignment, not estimates.

timelines.label: VEL-VIV-CELEB-GS-01 - as built
timelines.source: 58.5s, 18 cuts, avg 3.25s - one shared VO, three creators

beats.script: Okay, so if you love that Katie Holmes,
beats.visual: STILL, hard hold, zero camera move. Katie Holmes on the tarmac, chocolate top-handle in her hand.
beats.emotion: recognition - HOOK. She stops the scroll because she already knows this woman and already wants this bag.

beats.visual: STILL, hard hold. Sofia Richie in the rain, oxblood top-handle in her hand.
beats.emotion: confirmation - HOOK PART 2. Two names makes it a pattern, not a coincidence. The look has a category now.

beats.script: always in a Birkin shape bag, never a logo,
beats.visual: Our chocolate Vivienne on an unmade bed. Full trapezoid, clean front.
beats.emotion: quiet recognition - THE BRIDGE. Same shape, our bag, no announcement. Katie's bag was chocolate too and we never say so.

beats.script: quiet luxury written all over it, you already know the problem.
beats.visual: Shoulder strap, walking away down a hallway, bag moulding against her hip.
beats.emotion: aspiration turning to friction - PROBLEM SET-UP. 'You already know the problem' names the objection before she can.

beats.script: Every bag that gives you that look
beats.visual: Back to Sofia's still with the burned $10,000+ card over it.
beats.emotion: sticker shock - THE GUT PUNCH. The card does the work; the VO never names a house.

beats.visual: HARD CUT to our bag on a kitchen counter next to keys, a mug and a receipt.
beats.emotion: relief - THE ARGUMENT IS THE CUT. Ten-thousand-dollar object, then the same shape lying by a receipt.

beats.script: So I hunted down the affordable version.
beats.visual: Hand reaches in and grabs it off the entryway bench.
beats.emotion: discovery - SHE FOUND IT, not the brand. The creator is the finder, that is the whole trust mechanic.

beats.script: It's called the Vivienne by Velantra.
beats.visual: Hung over a chair back under a single table lamp. The beauty frame.
beats.emotion: arrival - PRODUCT INTRO. The name lands over the most flattering frame in the library.

beats.script: Same silhouette, no logo, actually accessible.
beats.visual: Riding on the passenger seat, daylight through the glass.
beats.emotion: permission - THE POSITIONING LINE. 'Actually accessible' is the promise the offer will pay off.

beats.script: It's vegetable tanned leather all the way through,
beats.visual: Fingers press flat into the front panel, natural pore grain, matte to satin.
beats.emotion: material trust - ATTRIBUTE 1. Touch proves hide. The press is the claim.

beats.script: with an aged brass belted turn lock,
beats.visual: Fingers turning the brass lock closed, macro.
beats.emotion: craft - ATTRIBUTE 2. Mechanism demonstrated, not described.
beats.note: The only cut where a mechanism actually moves. Let it complete.

beats.visual: Braided whip-stitch trim along the band, overhead macro.
beats.emotion: detail - ATTRIBUTE 3. The thing a cheap bag cannot fake.
beats.note: Shortest cut in the ad. Snap in, snap out.

beats.script: and zero branding anywhere on it.
beats.visual: The whole clean front panel lifted into the light, bare leather, hand clear of frame.
beats.emotion: quiet superiority - ATTRIBUTE 4 and the brand's thesis. The absence IS the feature.
beats.note: SHIPPED THE FALLBACK, not the GAP-02 macro - see the note on the board.

beats.script: It's soft, so instead of sitting stiff on your arm
beats.visual: The bag collapsed into the duvet, sides folded, holding no shape at all.
beats.emotion: reassurance - THE DIFFERENTIATOR OPENS. Every bag in this shape is rigid. Ours is not.
beats.note: Replaces the storyboard's second press frame, which twinned with 0:27.7 when built.

beats.script: like most bags in this shape,
beats.visual: Handles released, the bag drops and settles.
beats.emotion: contrast - THE DISMISSAL. The stiff-bag insult is spoken over OUR bag doing the opposite.
beats.note: Never cut to a competitor bag for a dismissal. The slump is the rebuttal.

beats.script: it slouches and molds to you as you carry it.
beats.visual: On the hip, walking, body moulding to her as she moves.
beats.emotion: ownership - SHE CAN SEE HERSELF CARRYING IT. Last emotional beat before the offer.

beats.script: And right now they've actually just opened pre orders on it.
beats.visual: Walking out the front door, bag in hand, blown daylight ahead.
beats.emotion: forward motion - THE TURN INTO THE OFFER.
beats.note: Last piece of b-roll. Everything after this is the website.

beats.script: Twenty five percent off, one forty nine instead of one ninety nine, and the first run ships in October. I've left the link below.
beats.visual: Live PDP screen recording. ONE unbroken scroll: price and swatches, Add to Cart, then the October pre-order paragraph, which settles and HOLDS.
beats.emotion: decision - OFFER AND CTA. The ad ends on the website and never cuts back to the bag.

notes.title: v2 - PRICE BEAT REBUILT (reused still + cheap card, both gone)
notes.text: v1 played the Sofia still a SECOND time with a burned $10,000+ graphic over it. The still had already run 8 seconds earlier as the hook, so it read as a reuse, and the card was doing work the voiceover already does. Both deleted. The whole price line now plays over ONE continuous cut of our bag on the kitchen counter, and the number lands in the ordinary word-synced caption instead of a graphic. Each celebrity still now appears EXACTLY ONCE. The ad is 17 cuts, not 18.

notes.title: v2 - VOICEOVER RE-RENDERED, the pause is gone
notes.text: Brooks heard a pause around the brand name. Measured: the read sits at a 0.060s median gap between words, but 'by' had a 0.19s gap and the brand word a 0.20s gap - three times normal - and both brand words were stretched. Cause was my own TTS respellings: eleven_v3 reads a hyphen as a syllable break, so 'Viv-ee-EN' and 'Vell-Ahn-Trah' got stretched AND given a pause on each side. Now fed plain as 'Vivian' and 'Vehlantra', which the caption map turns back into 'It's called the Vivienne by Velantra' on screen. Gaps are back at the median. EAR-CHECK THE BRAND WORD: ElevenLabs Scribe transcribes 'Volantra' for every spelling including the one that has been shipping, so it cannot judge that word - the test only proves going plain causes no regression and is tighter.

notes.title: PiP - the creator is CUT BY THE FRAME EDGE
notes.text: v1 had her floating in the corner as a complete cutout - a sticker on the b-roll. The bug was sizing the PiP on the PLATE (the inherited '32% of frame width' rule) when our creator keyframes were generated wide and waist-up, so her head came out tiny and her full outline showed. Measured off the shipped GS-BIRKIN-01 and BLK-01 ads: the house sizes on the HEAD (~20% of frame width, top at ~y1300) and lets the frame crop her on TWO edges. She now runs 60px below the bottom and 64-73px past the near side. Captions sit at y1120 to clear her.

notes.title: THREE FINISHED ADS - A / B / C
notes.text: Diane 58, Bridget 53, Marguerite 62. One shared voiceover drives all three, so the bed, the captions and every timing are identical and ONLY the creator changes - a clean creator-only test. Shipped with the words 'clean girl' cut from the hook, so the line reads 'that Katie Holmes, Sofia Richie energy' and a 62 year old is not saying 'clean girl'. Say the word and a fresh 35-45 trio is a re-render on the same VO.

notes.title: RUNTIME MOVED: 46.5s -> 58.5s
notes.text: The storyboard estimate assumed 180 wpm. This read came back at ~152. Nothing was cut and nothing was sped up - the one-take and no-atempo laws both say the read ships as-is, so the bed stretched to fit her. Average cut is 3.25s, inside the range GS-BIRKIN-01 shipped at.

notes.title: GAP-02 WAS NOT GENERATED - THE FALLBACK SHIPPED
notes.text: The seed the spec called for is the real unboxing frame, and it carries an ATORIE hang tag and the source listing's hardware, not ours. Seeding a 'zero branding anywhere on it' macro from a frame with a brand tag in it is the wrong move, and every other real frame has the same problem. 0:34.8 is the approved fallback instead: the clean front panel lifted into the light, hand clear. If you want the dedicated macro it needs a clean-room generation off the identity block, not an i2i - a separate job.

notes.title: FIXED DURING THE BUILD
notes.text: Three things the storyboard could not have known. (1) 0:37.4 was a second copy of the press-the-leather clip and twinned badly once built - it is now the bag collapsed into the duvet, a better frame for that line anyway. (2) The caption builder was merging short cards across sentence ends and produced one EIGHT-SECOND card spanning two cuts; it now breaks sentence to phrase to card and caps at 2.9s. (3) Cards sat at y=1500 and collided with the keyed creator's head, and had no scrim over the white PDP - they now sit at y=1330 with a feathered scrim measured on each line's own ink.

notes.title: STILL OPEN FOR YOU
notes.text: 1. The first-run scarcity line is still NOT in the ad. The '50,000 waitlist' and 'sold out seven times' were the reference ad's fabricated numbers. If it is true that the price returns to $199.99 after the first run, that line goes in and the VO re-renders. 2. Both hook frames are unlicensed press photography of real people. The ad never claims either carries ours, but it is worth your eyes before Meta review.

notes.title: DON'T
notes.text: Do not cut to a competitor bag for the 'most bags in this shape' dismissal - the insult is spoken over OUR bag doing the opposite. Do not put 'Birkin' in any generation prompt, ever; it lives in VO and captions only. Do not use the cafe-floor clip - she would not set a leather bag on a cafe floor. Do not cut back to the bag after the website.
